s1a: A buyer opens a PayPal dispute. Never got my parcel.
s1b: What the seller does in the next few days decides what it costs.
s2a: Refund, and the money goes back, the item is gone, and PayPal keeps its fee.
s2b: Settle it while it's still a dispute, and PayPal charges nothing.
s2c: Let it become a claim and lose, and PayPal adds a fee. Fourteen euros. For a busy shop, twenty-eight, even when it wins.
s3a: A one-person shop does this alone, in PayPal's own dashboard. Bigger shops put someone on it.
s3b: The tools that exist are built for card chargebacks, and many take a quarter of what they win back.
s4a: Second Look works inside those first days, while a dispute is still cheap. It pulls the evidence from PayPal, runs the ten checks a specialist would, and shows what each way out would cost, before you choose.
s4b: And it isn't only about money. The answer is ready in under a minute: polite, correct, and about this buyer's claim.
s4c: A seller who is clearly there reassures an honest buyer, and gives a dishonest one a reason to think twice.
s5a: Here it is live, on PayPal's sandbox. Opened under four minutes after paying: a calm reply, no refund.
s5b: When the parcel ships, it takes a fresh look, and sends the tracking to PayPal as proof.
s6a: Now a busier shop: two people, seventeen hundred orders in ninety days. Made-up data, same code.
s6b: This buyer took two of his three earlier disputes to a claim. The parcel was delivered to his PayPal address, so that proof goes to PayPal now.
s6c: It tells you when you're wrong, too. A return arrived, the refund never went out: the buyer is right. That refund is above your limit, so it comes back to you.
s6d: A pulled thread on a napkin: first, a photo. A parcel stuck for two weeks: refund it.
s6e: At a glance: how every case ended, and what the open ones could still cost.
s6f: It has its own screen, but your shop already works somewhere: a helpdesk, a team chat, a CRM. So it connects both ways.
s6g: Your systems can read a case, ask for a review, and approve it, under the same limits. And Second Look tells them when an answer has gone out.
s7a: Your limits, written in code, have the last word. More careful, never more generous. And nothing moves until you approve.
s8a: A few cents a dispute. Second Look. Sell without fear.
